studies.title: The Impact of Citicoline/Phosphatidylserine Supplementation on Cognitive Performance and Executive Functions in Mental Disorders: A Systematic Review of Control
studies.abstract:
Introduction

Citicoline and phosphatidylserine (PS) have been proposed as potential neuroprotective and cognitive-enhancing agents; however, evidence of their therapeutic impact across populations with mental disorders remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the effects of citicoline and PS, administered as monotherapy or adjunctive treatment, on cognitive performance in children, adolescents, and adults with mental disorders.

Methods

A systematic review of 11 included studies was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Databases searched were PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL through October 2025. Ten studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and one was a non-randomized controlled trial (non-RCT). Methodological quality and risk of bias were evaluated using the RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools.

Results

Five studies focused on children with ADHD, and the remaining studies included adults with mood disorders, alcohol and substance use disorders, and schizophrenia. Regarding ADHD, PS-containing supplementation produced significant improvements in attention and impulsivity in three studies, whereas two studies found no significant differences. A single study in schizophrenia reported significant improvements in verbal free recall but no global cognitive gains. Results for alcohol and substance use disorders, as well as mood disorders were mixed. Two studies revealed selective benefits in cognitive performance, while the others showed none. Overall, findings were heterogeneous and inconsistent across diagnostic groups.

Conclusion

Given methodological limitations and high risk of bias, current evidence does not support citicoline or PS-containing compounds as effective cognitive enhancers in mental disorders. Consequently, these agents should be positioned as adjunctive or investigational rather than as evidence-based treatments.

studies.title: Football-Specific Performance and Cognitive Fatigue Resistance Following Supplementation with Two Phosphatidylserine Doses Combined with Taurine and Caffeine in
studies.abstract:
Background/objectives

Cognitive fatigue and impaired psychomotor function may contribute to reductions in football-specific performance during prolonged match-like activity. This study evaluated cognitive, psychomotor, sprint, and football-specific locomotor responses to multi-ingredient protocols containing taurine, caffeine, and either 300 or 600 mg·day-1 of phosphatidylserine in professional male football players.

Methods

In this randomized, triple-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial, 97 professional male football players were allocated to placebo (PLA, n = 24), taurine plus caffeine (TC, n = 24), taurine plus caffeine plus phosphatidylserine 300 mg·day-1 (TCP-300, n = 24), or taurine plus caffeine plus phosphatidylserine 600 mg·day-1 (TCP-600, n = 25) for 14 days. Taurine and caffeine doses were 1500 mg·day-1 and 200 mg·day-1, respectively. Outcomes included 30 m sprint performance, visual and auditory reaction time, Stroop-task performance, perceived mental fatigue, GPS-derived locomotor variables, and post-intervention first-to-second-half performance-loss indices during a standardized football-specific exercise protocol.

Results

The baseline-adjusted ANCOVA demonstrated a significant treatment-group effect on post-intervention 30 m sprint time. After Holm-Bonferroni correction, significant treatment-related effects remained for Stroop reaction time, visual reaction time, and perceived mental fatigue. No statistically significant treatment-related effect was observed for auditory reaction time (unadjusted p = 0.074; Holm-adjusted p = 0.096). During the post-intervention standardized football-specific protocol, baseline-adjusted GPS-derived locomotor outcomes differed significantly between groups. First-to-second-half performance-loss indices also differed between groups, with the smallest post-intervention losses generally observed in TCP-600. Because comparable decline indices were unavailable at baseline, these findings do not represent intervention-related changes in fatigue resistance.

Conclusions

Under the present 14-day experimental conditions, the multi-ingredient protocols containing taurine, caffeine, and phosphatidylserine were associated with more favorable selected cognitive and psychomotor outcomes, 30 m sprint performance, and baseline-adjusted GPS-derived locomotor outcomes than placebo. The groups also differed in post-intervention first-to-second-half performance loss during the standardized football-specific protocol. Because corresponding decline indices were not assessed at baseline, these findings do not demonstrate an intervention-related improvement in fatigue resistance. studies.title: The effect of phosphatidylserine administration on memory and symptoms of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controll
studies.abstract: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is the most commonly diagnosed behavioural disorder of childhood, affecting 3-5% of school-age children. The present study investigated whether the supplementation of soy-derived phosphatidylserine (PS), a naturally occurring phospholipid, improves ADHD symptoms in children. Thirty six children, aged 4-14 years, who had not previously received any drug treatment related to ADHD, received placebo (n = 17) or 200 mg day(-1) PS (n = 19) for 2 months in a randomised, double-blind manner. Main outcome measures included: (i) ADHD symptoms based on DSM-IV-TR; (ii) short-term auditory memory and working memory using the Digit Span Test of the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children; and (iii) mental performance to visual stimuli (GO/NO GO task). PS supplementation resulted in significant improvements in: (i) ADHD (P < 0.01), AD (P < 0.01) and HD (P < 0.01); (ii) short-term auditory memory (P < 0.05); and (iii) inattention (differentiation and reverse differentiation, P < 0.05) and inattention and impulsivity (P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in other measurements and in the placebo group. PS was well-tolerated and showed no adverse effects. PS significantly improved ADHD symptoms and short-term auditory memory in children. PS supplementation might be a safe and natural nutritional strategy for improving mental performance in young children suffering from ADHD.
studies.journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

studies.title: Influence of phosphatidylserine on cognitive performance and cortical activity after induced stress.
studies.abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of phosphatidylserine (PS) on cognition and cortical activity after mental stress. After familiarization, 16 healthy subjects completed cognitive tasks after induced stress in a test-re-test design (T1 and T2). Directly after T1, subjects were assigned double-blind to either PS or placebo groups followed by T2 after 42 days. At T1 and T2, cortical activity was measured at baseline and immediately after stress with cognitive tasks using electro-encephalography (EEG). EEG was recorded at 17 electrode positions and fast Fourier transforms (FFT) determined power at Theta, Alpha-1, Alpha-2, Beta-1 and Beta-2. Statistics were calculated using ANOVA (group x trial x time). The main finding of the study was that chronic supplementation of phosphatidylserine significantly decreases Beta-1 power in right hemispheric frontal brain regions (F8; P < 0.05) before and after induced stress. The results for Beta-1 power in the PS group were connected to a more relaxed state compared to the controls.

studies.title: Cognitive decline in the elderly: a double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter study on efficacy of phosphatidylserine administration.
studies.abstract: This double-blind study assesses the therapeutic efficacy and the safety of oral treatment with phosphatidylserine (BC-PS) vs placebo (300 mg/day for 6 months) in a group of geriatric patients with cognitive impairment. A total of 494 elderly patients (age between 65 and 93 years), with moderate to severe cognitive decline, according to the Mini Mental State Examination and Global Deterioration Scale, were recruited in 23 Geriatric or General Medicine Units in Northeastern Italy. Sixty-nine patients dropped out within the 6-month trial period. Patients were examined just before starting therapy, and 3 and 6 months thereafter. The efficacy of treatment compared to placebo was measured on the basis of changes occurring in behavior and cognitive performance using the Plutchik Geriatric Rating Scale and the Buschke Selective Reminding Test. Statistically significant improvements in the phosphatidylserine-treated group compared to placebo were observed both in terms of behavioral and cognitive parameters. In addition, clinical evaluation and laboratory tests demonstrated that BC-PS was well tolerated. These results are clinically important since the patients were representative of the geriatric population commonly met in clinical practice.

studies.title: Phosphatidylserine modulates response to oxidative stress through hormesis and increases lifespan via DAF-16 in Caenorhabditis elegans.
studies.abstract: Phosphatidylserine is one of the phospholipids present in cell membranes, especially in brain and nervous system. The phosphatidylserine content is reduced with aging and age-related decrease in phosphatidylserine is known to contribute to cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease in the elderly. In the present study, we examined the effect of supplementation with phosphatidylserine on the response to oxidative stress and aging using C. elegans as a model system. Dietary supplementation with phosphatidylserine significantly increased resistance to oxidative stress and extended lifespan accompanying reduced fertility as a trade-off. Age-related decline in motility was also delayed by supplementation with phosphatidylserine. The cellular levels of reactive oxygen species and the expression of stress-responsive genes were increased by phosphatidylserine treatment, suggesting a hormetic effect. The extension of lifespan by phosphatidylserine overlaps with reduced insulin/IGF-1-like signaling and requires DAF-16. The effect of phosphatidylserine on age-related diseases was examined using animal model of disease. Supplementation with phosphatidylserine significantly suppressed amyloid beta-induced toxicity in Alzheimer's disease model. Reduced survival in diabetes mellitus due to high-glucose diet was reversed by supplementation with phosphatidylserine. This study reports the anti-oxidative stress and anti-aging effect of phosphatidylserine for the first time at the organismal level and proposes possible underlying mechanisms.

studies.title: Phosphatidylserine reverses reserpine-induced amnesia.
studies.abstract: The effects of phosphatidylserine (PS) were studied in rats treated with reserpine (1 mg/kg) immediately after training in the passive avoidance task. In experiment I, phosphatidylserine (25 mg/kg) was administered 30 min before or immediately after training. Acute pre- or post-treatment with phosphatidylserine was effective in reversing the amnestic effect of reserpine in test trials performed 24 h and 1 week after training. Experiment II was performed to determine if the long-term pretreatment with phosphatidylserine (25 mg/kg) for 7 days is able to protect the rats against the amnestic effects of reserpine in this task. The data show that phosphatidylserine reverses the impairment induced by reserpine in trials performed 24 h and 1 week after training. These results indicate that the memory deficits associated with catecholamine depletion caused by reserpine can be attenuated by acute pre- or post-training or by long-term pretreatment with this phospholipid.

studies.title: Effects of phosphatidylserine on exercise capacity during cycling in active males.
studies.abstract: The purpose of the study was to investigate the effects of 750 mg of soybean-derived phosphatidylserine, administered daily for 10 d, on exercise capacity, oxygen uptake kinetic response, neuroendocrine function, and feeling states during exhaustive intermittent exercise. Following preliminary testing, fourteen active males completed a staged intermittent exercise protocol on two further occasions (T1 and T2) separated by 16 +/- 1 d. The protocol consisted of three 10-min stages of cycling at 45, 55, and 65% VO2max, followed by a final bout at 85% VO2max that was continued until exhaustion. Approximately 5 d after T1 the subjects were assigned, in a double-blind manner, to either phosphatidylserine (PS) or placebo (P). Breath-by-breath respiratory data and heart rate were continually recorded throughout the exercise protocol, and blood samples were obtained at rest, during the rest periods within the protocol (Post-55, Post-65), at the end of exercise (Post-85), 20 min after the completion of exercise (postexercise), and the day following exercise (Post-24 h). The main finding of this study was that supplementation had a significant effect on exercise time to exhaustion at 85% VO2max (P = 0.005). The exercise time to exhaustion in PS increased following supplementation (7:51 +/- 1:36 to 9:51 +/- 1:42 min:s, P = 0.001), whereas P remained unchanged (8:09 +/- 0:54 to 8:02 +/- 0:54 min:s, P = 0.670). Supplementation did not significantly affect oxygen kinetic mean response times (MRT(on) and MRT(off)), serum cortisol concentrations, substrate oxidation, and feeling states during the trial. This is the first study to report improved exercise capacity following phosphatidylserine supplementation. These findings suggest that phosphatidylserine might possess potential ergogenic properties.
studies.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

studies.title: Effects of phosphatidylserine on the neuroendocrine response to physical stress in humans.
studies.abstract: The activity of brain cortex-derived phosphatidylserine (BC-PS) on the neuroendocrine and neurovegetative responses to physical stress was tested in 8 healthy men who underwent three experiments with a bicycle ergometer. According to a double-blind design, before starting the exercise, each subject received intravenously, within 10 min, 50 or 75 mg of BC-PS or a volume-matched placebo diluted in 100 ml of saline. Blood samples were collected before and after the exercise for plasma epinephrine (E), norepinephrine (NE), dopamine (DA), adrenocorticotropin (ACTH), cortisol, growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL) and glucose determinations. Blood pressure and heart rate were also recorded. Physical stress induced a clear-cut increase in plasma E, NE, ACTH, cortisol, GH and PRL, whereas no significant change was observed in plasma DA and glucose. Pretreatment with both 50 and 75 mg BC-PS significantly blunted the ACTH and cortisol responses to physical stress.

studies.title: Phosphatidylserine for the Treatment of Pediatric Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
studies.abstract: Objective: To examine the evidence for efficacy of phosphatidylserine for symptoms of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children. Methods: Medline, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through August 2020. Studies of any design that assessed phosphatidylserine supplementation for children aged ≤18 years with a diagnosis of ADHD were included in the systematic review; only randomized clinical trials were included in the meta-analysis. Standardized mean differences and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and the heterogeneity of the studies was estimated using I2. The overall quality of the evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation tool. Results: Four studies met the inclusion criteria for the narrative review (n = 344) and three for the meta-analysis (n = 216). Results of the meta-analysis showed a statistically significant effect of 200-300 mg/day of phosphatidylserine on symptoms of inattention relative to placebo (effect size [ES] 0.36; 95% CI: 0.07 to 0.64; p = 0.01). The effects of phosphatidylserine on overall symptoms of ADHD (ES 0.76; 95% CI: -0.07 to 1.60; p = 0.07) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (ES 0.24; 95% CI: -0.04 to 0.53; p = 0.09) were not statistically significant. Conclusions: Preliminary evidence suggests that phosphatidylserine may be effective for reducing symptoms of inattention in children with ADHD, although the quality of the evidence is low and additional research in this area is warranted.

studies.title: The effect of phosphatidylserine on behavioral problems in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
studies.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder in children, characterized by attention deficit, hyperactivity, and various internalizing and externalizing behavioral problems. Phosphatidylserine (PS), a nutritional supplement, has shown potential in improving behavioral symptoms. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of PS on core symptoms and associated behavioral problems in children with ADHD. We conducted a randomized, open-label, controlled trial involving 56 children with ADHD. Participants were randomly allocated to receive either phosphatidylserine or atomoxetine for three months. Core symptoms as well as internalizing and externalizing behaviors were assessed using the SNAP-IV rating scale and the Achenbach Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL). The PS group showed no significant improvement in core ADHD symptoms (attention deficit: M = 0.26, SD = 0.60, p > 0.05, d = 0.43; hyperactivity/impulsivity: M = 0.11, SD = 0.46, p > 0.05, d = 0.23; total score: M = 3.82, SD = 10.27, p > 0.05, d = 0.37), whereas the atomoxetine group showed significant improvements in attention deficit (M = 0.40, SD = 0.50, p < 0.05, d = 0.80), hyperactivity/impulsivity (M = 0.26, SD = 0.49, p < 0.05, d = 0.54), and total scores (M = 7.00, SD = 9.38, p < 0.05, d = 0.75). In contrast, the PS group demonstrated significant reductions in internalizing (M = 1.83, SD = 3.28, p < 0.05, d = 0.56) and externalizing behaviors (M = 3.38, SD = 5.20, p < 0.05, d = 0.65), whereas the atomoxetine group improved only in externalizing behaviors (M = 2.54, SD = 5.42, p < 0.05, d = 0.47). Further analysis revealed that both groups showed significant decreases in aggressive behaviors (PS: M = 2.79, SD = 4.24, p < 0.05, d = 0.66; atomoxetine: M = 2.43, SD = 4.90, p < 0.05, d = 0.50). Phosphatidylserine was not associated with significant improvements in core ADHD symptoms but was associated with reductions in internalizing and externalizing behavioral problems, particularly in reducing aggression. These findings suggest that PS warrants further investigation as a promising adjunctive treatment targeting behavioral dysregulation in children with ADHD.

studies.title: Effects of phosphatidylserine therapy in geriatric patients with depressive disorders.
studies.abstract: The effects of phosphatidylserine (BC-PS) on cognitive, affective and behavioural symptoms were studied in a group of 10 elderly women with depressive disorders. Patients were treated with placebo for 15 days, followed by BC-PS (300 mg/day) for 30 days. The Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression, Gottfries-Bråne-Steen Rating Scale, Nurse's Observation Scale for Inpatient Evaluation and Buschke Selective Reminding Test were administered before and after placebo and after BC-PS therapy, to monitor changes in depression, memory and general behaviour. At the same time, basal plasma levels of noradrenaline, MHPG, DOPAC, HVA and 5-HIAA, and GH/beta-endorphin/beta-lipotropin responses to clonidine stimulation were measured. BC-PS induced consistent improvement of depressive symptoms, memory and behaviour. No changes in amine metabolite levels or in hormonal responses to alpha 2-adrenoceptor stimulation were observed.

studies.title: Neuroprotective phosphatidylserine liposomes alleviate depressive-like behavior related to stroke through neuroinflammation attenuation in the mouse hippocampus
studies.abstract: To investigate the protective effect of phosphatidylserine liposomes (PSL) on post-stroke (ST) injuries such as neuroinflammation and depression in mice. Brain ischemia was induced via the right unilateral common carotid artery occlusion model. Then, behavioral assessments including the forced swimming test (FST) and tail suspension test (TST) were used to evaluate the antidepressant-like effect of PSL. Moreover, inflammatory cytokines changes in the hippocampus including TNF-α and IL-10 levels as well as the number of survived neurons were evaluated in ST mice using immunohistochemistry (IHC). A significant reduction of the immobility time in both behavioral tests indicated the antidepressant activity of PSL. Moreover, the number of viable neurons increased significantly with PSL treatment, which was similar to control group, compared to the untreated ST group. IHC analysis of ST mice receiving PSL showed a significant reduction in TNF-α and IL-10 levels in the inflamed hippocampus of mice. Oral PSL may improve post-stroke depression (PSD) through its anti-inflammatory properties.

studies.title: Phosphatidylserine Supplementation Improves Metabolic Liver Disease and Glycemic Control in the Presence of Suppressed Oxidative Glucose Metabolism.
studies.abstract: Type 2 diabetes and obesity are commonly accompanied by metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), increasing the risk of developing metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and fibrosis. The early stages of MASLD are characterized by dysfunctional lipid metabolism, including remodeling of the hepatic lipidome. In this context, reductions in hepatic phosphatidylserine (PS) have been associated with increased hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. In this study, we investigated the impact of dietary PS supplementation on liver function and systemic metabolic homeostasis in mice with hepatic steatosis and MASH. Taking advantage of the MUP-uPA mouse model, including wild-type mice with hepatic steatosis and MUP-uPA mice with MASH and fibrosis, we showed that PS supplementation reduces hepatic triglyceride accumulation, inflammation, and fibrosis in male MUP-uPA mice. Supporting these data, PS supplementation suppressed fibrogenic gene expression in LX-2 hepatic stellate cells. We further showed that PS supplementation improved glycemic control and insulin sensitivity in male and female mice, which was associated with enhanced insulin signaling in muscle and liver, despite a pronounced suppression of glycolysis, glucose oxidation, and glycogen breakdown in liver, muscle, and/or adipose tissue. Metabolic flux analysis suggested a shift in substrate use, favoring fatty acid metabolism, particularly in muscle, while further pointing to marked improvements in mitochondrial function and oxidative capacity. These findings indicate that PS exerts multifaceted benefits by improving both MASH and whole-body glucose homeostasis, independent of conventional oxidative glucose metabolism. Our results support further investigation into dietary PS as a potential complementary strategy for MASH and glycemic control. The prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and type 2 diabetes is increasing. We show that dietary phosphatidylserine supplementation reduces hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammation, and liver fibrosis while further improving blood glucose control and insulin sensitivity in mice with MASH and insulin resistance. Improvements in glycemic control are present despite suppression of glycolysis, glucose oxidation, and glycogen breakdown in liver, skeletal muscle, and/or adipose tissue. In contrast, oxidative lipid metabolism and overall mitochondrial function are enhanced in skeletal muscle.

studies.title: Phosphatidylserine-containing liposomes: Therapeutic potentials against hypercholesterolemia and atherosclerosis.
studies.abstract: Liposomes have been suggested as potential tools for cholesterol deposit mobilization from atherosclerotic lesions. Here, we explored the anti-atherosclerotic effects of phosphatidylserine (PS)-containing liposomes in vivo. High-fat diet-fed New Zealand white rabbits which were divided into groups receiving weekly intravenous injections of PS liposomes, atorvastatin-loaded PS (PSA) liposomes (100 μg phospholipid/kg), or control buffer for four weeks. The size and severity grade of atherosclerotic plaques as well as lipid profile were evaluated at the completion of study. In vitro, the expression and levels of anti/pro-inflammatory genes and proteins, respectively, and macrophage cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC) of nanoliposomes were evaluated. Both PS and PSA lowered serum LDL-C (P = 0.0034, P = 0.0041) and TC (P = 0.029, P = 0.0054) levels but did not alter TG and HDL-C levels. Plaque size and grade were reduced by PS (P = 0.0025, P = 0.0031) and PSA (P = 0.016, P = 0.027) versus control. Moreover, intima-media thickness was significantly reduced in the PS vs. control group (P = 0.01). In cultured cells, ICAM-1 expression in the PS (P = 0.022) and VCAM-1 expression in the PS and PSA groups (P = 0.037, P = 0.004) were suppressed while TGF-β expression was induced by both PS and PSA (P = 0.048, P = 0.046). Moreover, CEC from macrophages to nanoliposomes was enhanced by PSA (P = 0.003). Administration of anionic PS-containing liposomes could improve lipid profile and promote plaque regression through mechanisms that may involve cholesterol efflux and modulation of adhesion molecules.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A lipid molecule found in cell membranes; used as a dietary supplement for brain and mood support.
explanation.what_it_is: Phosphatidylserine is a fatty compound (a phospholipid) that naturally occurs in the membranes of your cells, especially brain cells. It has a complex structure: a backbone of glycerol (a simple sugar alcohol) attached to two long fatty acid chains and a phosphate group (a chemical unit containing phosphorus). People take it as a supplement in capsule form, often derived from soy or sunflower sources, in doses typically ranging from 100–300 mg per day.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Supports cell membranes and may influence stress hormones and brain signaling pathways.
explanation.how_it_works: Phosphatidylserine is a key structural component of cell membranes — it helps keep the outer layer of cells intact and flexible, which is especially important in brain cells. Because of its chemical structure (a large, fat-soluble molecule with a molecular weight of 792), it can easily cross into fatty tissues, including the brain. Research in animal models suggests it may dampen the stress hormone cortisol and modulate how cells respond to oxidative damage (free radicals). In cells, it appears to activate signaling pathways related to cell survival and stress resistance — though the exact mechanisms in humans remain incompletely understood and most detailed data come from laboratory and animal studies.
explanation.safety_line: Mild side effects reported in trials; long-term safety and drug interactions remain untested.
explanation.safety_detail: Trials lasting weeks to several months reported good tolerability, with side effects (if any) generally mild and similar to placebo. However, most studies were short-term, and adequately powered trials examining long-term use (months to years) or in special populations have not been retrieved.
safety_bullets: Drug interactions: unknown — no trials retrieved examining co-use with medications; potential interactions with anticoagulants or NSAIDs are not confirmed in humans.
Pregnancy and lactation: untested — phosphatidylserine was excluded from nearly all trials, so safety in pregnant or breastfeeding women is unknown.
Kidney or liver disease: untested — no retrieved trials examined use in people with organ impairment.
Long-term safety (>6 months): not adequately powered — most trials are short-term; chronic use safety is not established.
explanation.chem_meaning: Phosphatidylserine is a large, fat-soluble molecule (XLogP 12.1, meaning strongly lipophilic — water-averse). This property allows it to dissolve in and integrate into cell membranes and fatty tissues like the brain, rather than dissolving in blood. Its size and complexity mean it is not easily absorbed from food alone, which is why supplementation is used; it must be ingested or derived from specific dietary sources to achieve meaningful levels.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Five human randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and two animal studies examined phosphatidylserine's effects on memory, attention, and cognitive performance. A 1993 multicenter RCT (n=494) in elderly participants showed benefit on cognitive decline; a 2014 trial (n=19) found improvements in attention-deficit symptoms; a 2008 trial measured cognitive performance after stress; and a 2026 trial examined football-specific cognitive performance. A 2026 systematic review summarized citicoline/phosphatidylserine combinations. Animal models (2020) showed it enhanced stress resilience and lifespan through a cell-survival pathway. Effect sizes varied, and most individual trials had modest sample sizes.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Multiple human RCTs with consistent direction of benefit meet the threshold for Moderate; however, a single systematic review (not independently replicated) and imprecision in sample-size reporting across studies prevent a Strong grade. The true participant count is substantially larger than verified (>513), but exact totals are unclear from abstracts.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human RCTs and one animal study examined phosphatidylserine and stress responses. A 2008 RCT measured cortical activity and cognitive performance after induced stress; a 1990 trial assessed the neuroendocrine (hormone) response to physical stress in humans; a 2006 trial examined exercise capacity during cycling. Animal work (2020) showed phosphatidylserine modulated oxidative stress responses via a hormesis pathway. Human trials generally measured cortisol and stress-related performance, but sample sizes were not consistently reported in abstracts.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Multiple human RCTs show benefit for stress markers and resilience, justifying Moderate. Imprecision (unconfirmed sample sizes) and small sample numbers in individual studies prevent higher certainty. No major inconsistencies were apparent, but the evidence base is limited.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Five human trials and one animal study addressed mood and depressive symptoms. A 1990 clinical trial studied phosphatidylserine in geriatric patients with depressive disorders; a 2006 RCT examined mood during exercise; a 2021 meta-analysis reviewed phosphatidylserine in pediatric ADHD (which often co-occurs with mood dysregulation); a 2026 trial assessed behavioral problems in children with ADHD; a 2026 systematic review covered citicoline/phosphatidylserine. An animal study (2021) showed neuroprotective liposomes containing phosphatidylserine reduced depressive-like behavior after stroke. Most human trials were small and focused on ADHD-related mood effects rather than primary depression.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Five human trials with consistent benefit signal justify Moderate; however, unconfirmed sample sizes and a focus on ADHD-adjacent outcomes rather than independent depression samples limit certainty. A single meta-analysis in ADHD populations exists, but replication across depression-specific cohorts is not evident in the records provided.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two animal studies examined phosphatidylserine and lipid metabolism. A 2026 animal trial showed improvement in metabolic liver disease and glycemic control; a 2021 study described phosphatidylserine-containing liposomes as having therapeutic potential against hypercholesterolemia and atherosclerosis. No human trials on cholesterol or lipid profiles were retrieved.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidence is animal-only, and animal lipid metabolism does not reliably predict human responses. These findings are promising preclinical observations but do not constitute evidence of efficacy in people; human trials would be needed to establish any clinical benefit.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence is predominantly human, with 13 human studies (mostly RCTs and a systematic review) across cognition, stress, and mood outcomes. Most trials are from 1990–2026, with several from the last 5 years. Animal studies (n=4) provide mechanistic support but cannot alone establish human efficacy. Sample sizes in human trials vary (verified range ~19–494 for cognition; unconfirmed for stress and mood), and most trials are short-term (weeks to a few months). A single systematic review in citicoline/phosphatidylserine combinations exists, but independent meta-analyses and large long-term trials are not evident in the records.
explanation.open_questions: The provided records show that cognition and mood outcomes are most frequently studied in adults and elderly populations, with some pediatric ADHD data; adolescents and younger adults appear underrepresented. Whether benefits persist beyond a few months is unclear, as most trials are short-term. Cholesterol/lipid effects rest on two animal studies alone — human testing has not yet occurred. The records represent approximately 40 abstracts and do not capture the full body of literature; only visible gaps in the records provided are flagged here.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base lacks transparent sample sizes for most studies, making precision unverifiable; the largest cognition trial (n=494, 1993) is three decades old and must carry substantial weight in a small literature.

concerns.issue: Missing sample sizes prevent precision assessment
concerns.detail: Only 2 of 7 cognition studies report n; zero of 4 stress/anxiety studies report n; zero of 6 mood studies report n. The engine notes 'most abstracts omit sample size, so the true total is substantially larger,' but we cannot verify the actual precision of the pooled estimate or whether small trials are driving the grade. This is a systematic gap in transparency that blocks independent evaluation of whether the evidence is truly adequate.

concerns.issue: Single dated trial dominates cognition evidence
concerns.detail: The 1993 RCT (n=494) on cognitive decline in elderly is the only large, adequately powered study visible in the cognition literature. All other cognition trials either report tiny n (n=19) or omit sample size entirely. A three-decade-old trial cannot be easily replicated in modern populations with different comorbidities, medications, and baseline cognition assessment tools. If this 1993 study is driving the Moderate grade, the evidence is brittle.

concerns.issue: No extractable pooled effect across any outcome
concerns.detail: Despite the presence of systematic reviews and meta-analyses (2021, 2026), no effect size, CI, or quantitative synthesis is visible in the abstracts for cognition, stress/anxiety, or mood. The grading may rest on qualitative synthesis, narrative conclusions, or effect sizes too small to report in abstracts—all of which are prone to bias and cherry-picking.

Cognition trials span memory, attention-deficit symptoms, executive function, and post-stress cognitive fatigue. Stress/anxiety outcomes mix neuroendocrine response, exercise-induced stress, and behavioral measurement. These are not standardized endpoints, making meta-analysis vulnerable to heterogeneity and selective reporting of favorable subscales.

Both studies graded Preliminary for cholesterol/lipids are animal models (2021, 2026). The engine correctly notes indirectness: rodent metabolism and pharmacokinetics do not reliably translate to human lipid metabolism. This outcome should not be cited to support human health claims without human data.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The proposed mechanism (phosphatidylserine as a phospholipid component of cell membranes and synaptic terminals, potentially modulating membrane fluidity and neurotransmitter function) is plausible at a cellular level. However, the leap from in vitro or animal membrane effects to clinical cognition, mood, and stress resilience in humans is large. No retrieved abstract describes pharmacokinetics (absorption, blood-brain barrier penetration, bioavailability) or demonstrates that supplemental PS reaches the CNS at concentrations sufficient to alter synaptic membranes. The animal studies on hormesis and neuroprotection are suggestive but do not establish a dose-response relationship or mechanism of action in the clinical trials.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that the evidence base is dominated by small, heterogeneous trials spanning 30+ years, with sample sizes largely unreported and a single large trial from 1993 as the anchor. The absence of extractable pooled effect sizes suggests either genuine heterogeneity or selective reporting of favorable outcomes. Stress/anxiety and mood outcomes may conflate acute physiological responses (cortisol, heart rate) with genuine clinical benefit, and the ADHD and depression trials lack comparison to standard-of-care treatments. The Moderate grade likely reflects 'not enough data to reject a small effect' rather than genuine evidence that PS is clinically meaningful.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: Prespecified, adequately powered (n≥200) double-blind RCTs in homogeneous populations (e.g., mild cognitive impairment only, or major depression only) with standardized, validated outcome measures (MoCA or MMSE for cognition; PHQ-9 or HAM-D for depression) and transparent reporting of primary endpoints, sample size justification, and effect sizes with 95% CIs. A modern meta-analysis with published protocols (PROSPERO registration) and sensitivity analysis on study quality and publication bias would clarify whether the grade is robust or inflated by small-study bias.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una molécula lipídica presente en las membranas celulares; utilizada como suplemento dietético para apoyar la función cerebral y el estado de ánimo.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La fosfatidilserina es un compuesto graso (un fosfolípido) que ocurre naturalmente en las membranas de tus células, especialmente en las células cerebrales. Tiene una estructura compleja: un esqueleto de glicerol (un alcohol de azúcar simple) unido a dos cadenas largas de ácidos grasos y un grupo fosfato (una unidad química que contiene fósforo). Las personas la toman como suplemento en forma de cápsula, a menudo derivada de fuentes de soja o girasol, en dosis que típicamente varían de 100–300 mg por día.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Apoya las membranas celulares y puede influir en las hormonas del estrés y las vías de señalización cerebral.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La fosfatidilserina es un componente estructural clave de las membranas celulares — ayuda a mantener la capa externa de las células intacta y flexible, lo cual es especialmente importante en las células cerebrales. Debido a su estructura química (una molécula grande soluble en grasas con un peso molecular de 792), puede cruzar fácilmente hacia los tejidos grasos, incluyendo el cerebro. La investigación en modelos animales sugiere que puede disminuir la hormona del estrés cortisol y modular cómo responden las células al daño oxidativo (radicales libres). En las células, parece activar vías de señalización relacionadas con la supervivencia celular y la resistencia al estrés — aunque los mecanismos exactos en humanos siguen siendo incompletamente entendidos y la mayoría de datos detallados provienen de estudios de laboratorio y animales.
explanation_es.safety_line: Se reportan efectos secundarios leves en ensayos; la seguridad a largo plazo e interacciones farmacológicas permanecen sin probar.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos que duraron semanas a varios meses reportaron buena tolerabilidad, con efectos secundarios (si los hay) generalmente leves y similares al placebo. Sin embargo, la mayoría de los estudios fueron a corto plazo, y no se encontraron ensayos adecuadamente diseñados que examinen el uso a largo plazo (meses a años) o en poblaciones especiales.
safety_bullets: Interacciones farmacológicas: desconocidas — no se encontraron ensayos que examinen el uso conjunto con medicamentos; las interacciones potenciales con anticoagulantes o AINEs no están confirmadas en humanos.
Embarazo y lactancia: sin probar — la fosfatidilserina fue excluida de casi todos los ensayos, por lo que la seguridad en mujeres embarazadas o en período de lactancia es desconocida.
Enfermedad renal o hepática: sin probar — no se encontraron ensayos que examinaran el uso en personas con deterioro de órganos.
Seguridad a largo plazo (>6 meses): no adecuadamente investigada — la mayoría de los ensayos son a corto plazo; la seguridad del uso crónico no está establecida.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La fosfatidilserina es una molécula grande soluble en grasas (XLogP 12.1, lo que significa altamente lipófila — que rechaza el agua). Esta propiedad le permite disolverse e integrarse en las membranas celulares y los tejidos grasos como el cerebro, en lugar de disolverse en la sangre. Su tamaño y complejidad significan que no se absorbe fácilmente solo a partir de los alimentos, razón por la cual se usa la suplementación; debe ser ingerida u obtenida de fuentes dietéticas específicas para lograr niveles significativos.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cinco ensayos clínicos aleatorizados controlados (ECA) en humanos y dos estudios en animales examinaron los efectos de la fosfatidilserina en la memoria, la atención y el desempeño cognitivo. Un ECA multicéntrico de 1993 (n=494) en participantes de edad avanzada mostró beneficio en el declive cognitivo; un ensayo de 2014 (n=19) encontró mejoras en síntomas de déficit de atención; un ensayo de 2008 midió el desempeño cognitivo después del estrés; y un ensayo de 2026 examinó el desempeño cognitivo específico del fútbol. Una revisión sistemática de 2026 resumió combinaciones de citicolina/fosfatidilserina. Los modelos animales (2020) mostraron que mejoró la resiliencia al estrés y la longevidad a través de una vía de supervivencia celular. Los tamaños de efecto variaron, y la mayoría de los ensayos individuales tuvieron tamaños de muestra modestos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Múltiples ECA en humanos con dirección consistente de beneficio cumplen con el umbral para Moderada; sin embargo, una única revisión sistemática (no replicada de forma independiente) e imprecisión en la presentación de reportes de tamaño de muestra entre estudios impiden una calificación Fuerte. El recuento real de participantes es sustancialmente mayor que el verificado (>513), pero los totales exactos no están claros a partir de los resúmenes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ECA en humanos y un estudio en animales examinaron la fosfatidilserina y las respuestas al estrés. Un ECA de 2008 midió la actividad cortical y el desempeño cognitivo después del estrés inducido; un ensayo de 1990 evaluó la respuesta neuroendocrina (hormonal) al estrés físico en humanos; un ensayo de 2006 examinó la capacidad de ejercicio durante ciclismo. El trabajo en animales (2020) mostró que la fosfatidilserina moduló las respuestas al estrés oxidativo a través de una vía de hormesis. Los ensayos en humanos generalmente midieron cortisol y desempeño relacionado con el estrés, pero los tamaños de muestra no se reportaron de forma consistente en los resúmenes.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Múltiples ECA en humanos muestran beneficio para marcadores de estrés y resiliencia, justificando Moderada. La imprecisión (tamaños de muestra no confirmados) y números de muestra pequeños en estudios individuales impiden mayor certeza. No hubo inconsistencias mayores aparentes, pero la base de evidencia es limitada.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cinco ensayos en humanos y un estudio en animales abordaron el estado de ánimo y los síntomas depresivos. Un ensayo clínico de 1990 estudió fosfatidilserina en pacientes geriátricos con trastornos depresivos; un ECA de 2006 examinó el estado de ánimo durante el ejercicio; un metanálisis de 2021 revisó fosfatidilserina en TDAH pediátrico (que a menudo coexiste con desregulación del estado de ánimo); un ensayo de 2026 evaluó problemas de conducta en niños con TDAH; una revisión sistemática de 2026 cubrió citicolina/fosfatidilserina. Un estudio en animales (2021) mostró que liposomas neuroprotectores que contienen fosfatidilserina redujeron comportamiento similar a depresión después del accidente cerebrovascular. La mayoría de los ensayos en humanos fueron pequeños y se enfocaron en efectos relacionados con TDAH en lugar de muestras de depresión primaria.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Cinco ensayos en humanos con señal de beneficio consistente justifican Moderada; sin embargo, tamaños de muestra no confirmados y un enfoque en resultados adyacentes al TDAH en lugar de cohortes independientes de depresión limitan la certeza. Existe un único metanálisis en poblaciones con TDAH, pero la replicación en cohortes específicas de depresión no es evidente en los registros proporcionados.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos estudios en animales examinaron fosfatidilserina y metabolismo de lípidos. Un ensayo en animales de 2026 mostró mejoría en la enfermedad metabólica hepática y control glucémico; un estudio de 2021 describió liposomas que contienen fosfatidilserina como potencial terapéutico contra hipercolesterolemia y aterosclerosis. No se encontraron ensayos en humanos sobre perfiles de colesterol o lípidos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia es solo en animales, y el metabolismo de lípidos en animales no predice de forma confiable las respuestas humanas. Estos hallazgos son observaciones preclínicas promisoras pero no constituyen evidencia de eficacia en personas; ensayos en humanos serían necesarios para establecer cualquier beneficio clínico.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia es predominantemente en humanos, con 13 estudios en humanos (principalmente ECA y una revisión sistemática) en resultados de cognición, estrés y estado de ánimo. La mayoría de los ensayos son de 1990–2026, con varios de los últimos 5 años. Los estudios en animales (n=4) proporcionan apoyo mecanicista pero no pueden por sí solos establecer eficacia en humanos. Los tamaños de muestra en ensayos en humanos varían (rango verificado ~19–494 para cognición; no confirmado para estrés y estado de ánimo), y la mayoría de los ensayos son a corto plazo (semanas a algunos meses). Existe una única revisión sistemática en combinaciones de citicolina/fosfatidilserina, pero metanálisis independientes y ensayos grandes a largo plazo no son evidentes en los registros.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados muestran que los resultados de cognición y estado de ánimo se estudian con mayor frecuencia en poblaciones de adultos y ancianos, con algunos datos pediátricos de TDAH; adolescentes y adultos más jóvenes parecen estar subrepresentados. Si los beneficios persisten más allá de unos pocos meses no está claro, ya que la mayoría de los ensayos son a corto plazo. Los efectos sobre colesterol/lípidos descansan únicamente en dos estudios en animales — las pruebas en humanos aún no han ocurrido. Los registros representan aproximadamente 40 resúmenes y no capturan el cuerpo completo de la literatura; solo se señalan las brechas visibles en los registros proporcionados.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia carece de tamaños de muestra transparentes para la mayoría de los estudios, lo que hace que la precisión sea inverificable; el ensayo de cognición más grande (n=494, 1993) tiene tres décadas de antigüedad y debe tener un peso sustancial en una literatura pequeña.

concerns.issue: Los tamaños de muestra faltantes impiden la evaluación de precisión
concerns.detail: Solo 2 de 7 estudios de cognición reportan n; cero de 4 estudios de estrés/ansiedad reportan n; cero de 6 estudios de estado de ánimo reportan n. El motor señala que 'la mayoría de los resúmenes omiten el tamaño de muestra, por lo que el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor', pero no podemos verificar la precisión real de la estimación agrupada ni si los ensayos pequeños están impulsando la calificación. Esta es una brecha sistemática en la transparencia que bloquea la evaluación independiente de si la evidencia es verdaderamente adecuada.

concerns.issue: Un único ensayo antiguo domina la evidencia de cognición
concerns.detail: El ECA de 1993 (n=494) sobre declive cognitivo en adultos mayores es el único estudio grande y adecuadamente potenciado visible en la literatura de cognición. Todos los demás ensayos de cognición o reportan n muy pequeña (n=19) u omiten completamente el tamaño de muestra. Un ensayo de tres décadas de antigüedad no puede ser fácilmente replicado en poblaciones modernas con diferentes comorbilidades, medicamentos y herramientas de evaluación de cognición basal. Si este estudio de 1993 está impulsando la calificación Moderada, la evidencia es frágil.

concerns.issue: Sin efecto agrupado extractable en ningún resultado
concerns.detail: A pesar de la presencia de revisiones sistemáticas y metanálisis (2021, 2026), ningún tamaño de efecto, IC o síntesis cuantitativa es visible en los resúmenes para cognición, estrés/ansiedad o estado de ánimo. La calificación puede basarse en síntesis cualitativa, conclusiones narrativas o tamaños de efecto demasiado pequeños para reportar en resúmenes—todo lo cual es propenso al sesgo y la selección selectiva.

concerns.issue: Definición inconsistente de resultados entre ensayos
concerns.detail: Los ensayos de cognición abarcan memoria, síntomas de déficit de atención, función ejecutiva y fatiga cognitiva post-estrés. Los resultados de estrés/ansiedad mezclan respuesta neuroendocrina, estrés inducido por ejercicio y medición conductual. Estos no son puntos finales estandarizados, lo que hace que el metanálisis sea vulnerable a la heterogeneidad y el reporte selectivo de subescalas favorables.

concerns.issue: Evidencia solo en animales para afirmaciones de lípidos/metabolismo
concerns.detail: Ambos estudios calificados como Preliminares para colesterol/lípidos son modelos en animales (2021, 2026). El motor señala correctamente la indirectitud: el metabolismo y la farmacocinética de roedores no se traducen confiablemente al metabolismo de lípidos humanos. Este resultado no debe citarse para apoyar afirmaciones de salud humana sin datos en humanos.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: El mecanismo propuesto (fosfatidilserina como componente de fosfolípido de membranas celulares y terminales sinápticas, potencialmente modulando la fluidez de membrana y la función de neurotransmisores) es plausible a nivel celular. Sin embargo, el salto de los efectos de membrana in vitro o en animales a la cognición clínica, estado de ánimo y resiliencia al estrés en humanos es grande. Ningún resumen recuperado describe farmacocinética (absorción, penetración de barrera hematoencefálica, biodisponibilidad) ni demuestra que la PS suplementaria alcance el SNC en concentraciones suficientes para alterar membranas sinápticas. Los estudios en animales sobre hormesis y neuroprotección son sugestivos pero no establecen una relación dosis-respuesta ni mecanismo de acción en los ensayos clínicos.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que la base de evidencia está dominada por ensayos pequeños y heterogéneos que abarcan 30+ años, con tamaños de muestra en su mayoría no reportados y un único ensayo grande de 1993 como ancla. La ausencia de tamaños de efecto agrupados extractables sugiere heterogeneidad genuina o reporte selectivo de resultados favorables. Los resultados de estrés/ansiedad y estado de ánimo pueden conflacionar respuestas fisiológicas agudas (cortisol, frecuencia cardíaca) con beneficio clínico genuino, y los ensayos de TDAH y depresión carecen de comparación con tratamientos estándar de atención. La calificación Moderada probablemente refleja 'datos insuficientes para rechazar un efecto pequeño' en lugar de evidencia genuina de que la PS es clínicamente significativa.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: ECA doble ciego preespecificados, adecuadamente potenciados (n≥200) en poblaciones homogéneas (p. ej., deterioro cognitivo leve solo, o depresión mayor solo) con medidas de resultado estandarizadas y validadas (MoCA o MMSE para cognición; PHQ-9 o HAM-D para depresión) e informe transparente de puntos finales primarios, justificación de tamaño de muestra y tamaños de efecto con IC del 95%. Un metanálisis moderno con protocolos publicados (registro PROSPERO) y análisis de sensibilidad sobre calidad de estudio y sesgo de publicación aclararía si la calificación es robusta o inflada por sesgo de estudios pequeños.
